bull_bear.body: Pause on new M&A for 6-8 months to digest 7 recent acquisitions (3 MedTech); focus on organic ROIC improvement; put option liabilities recognized under IndAS impacting net worth presentation.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Minority interest volatility (normalized from 38% to ~25%); working capital cycle sensitivity to MedTech mix (higher receivable days); key person risk in acquired entities mitigated by 1-year lock-ins and skin-in-the-game.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'chewing' acquired assets over new deals; transparent on accounting distortions (put options, minority spikes); bullish on MedTech synergies.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Reported net worth flattish due to IndAS put option liability recognition rather than operational decline; Q4 minority interest spike was a one-off due to preponed government project sales in a partial-owned subsidiary; GLP-1 distribution is a hidden moat due to cold-chain barriers.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Acquisition structures embed staged buyouts: "The Company holds call options (subject to certain conditions) to acquire the residual minority stake in its subsidiaries over a pre-defined time horizon, exercisable at a valuation multiple consistent with the multiple paid at the time of the original acquisition."
- Balance sheet shows the roll-up's footprint — goodwill of Rs 749.1 Cr at Mar-26 versus Rs 424.0 Cr at Mar-25 and Rs 192.8 Cr at Mar-24.
- Funding mix shifted in FY26: non-current borrowings Rs 122.6 Cr (Mar-26) versus Rs 0.0 Cr (Mar-25), current borrowings Rs 444.1 Cr versus Rs 298.8 Cr.
- FY26 was the first year in the five-year series with positive Net Cash from Operating Activities (Rs 96.2 Cr, versus negative in FY22-FY25), against Net Cash used in Investing Activities of Rs -303.0 Cr.
- The deck states no dividend policy, buyback or payout philosophy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Scale and density of a pan-India network - 136 warehouses, 523 districts, 105,300+ retail pharmacies and 3,600+ hospitals - enabling timely availability and deep penetration into Tier-II/Tier-III geographies
- Breadth of catalogue: 97,500+ SKUs sourced from 3,300+ manufacturers, letting customers source a meaningful share of their basket from one supplier
- Depth of manufacturer relationships, translating into wider product access, better procurement terms and exclusive pan-India distribution partnerships in MedTech
- Proprietary technology stack (in-house ERP, Entero Direct, HealthEdge) giving real-time inventory visibility, better fill rates and a repeatable way to onboard acquired businesses
- A proven, repeatable acquisition and integration model - 45+ strategic acquisitions - with defined diligence, integration and value-creation levers (procurement consolidation, cost rationalisation, platform onboarding)
- Operating in a fragmented industry where roughly 90% of the market is still serviced by small region-specific distributors, giving an organised player with capital access a structural consolidation advantage
- Customer stickiness and rising wallet share driven by service reliability and product availability
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Product integrity in healthcare distribution — The business is exposed to distributing expired, defective or counterfeit products, transportation damage and customer returns, which could cause financial losses, reputational damage and product liability claims - and any claim, regardless of validity, can erode customer trust. Mitigation is buying directly from manufacturers meeting agreed quality standards, with defects replaced by the manufacturer.
- Operational disruption to warehouses and logistics — Any disruption to warehouse operations, or to the development of new warehousing and logistics facilities - including natural disasters or catastrophic events - could materially impact the business. Redundancy across a nationwide network of 100+ distribution warehouses is the stated buffer.
- M&A integration risk — Growth is acquisition-led, so failure to identify, complete and successfully integrate acquisitions, or acquisitions failing to deliver internal results, would directly hit financial performance. Mitigated by a dedicated M&A team targeting territorial expansion/dominance or unique product mix, plus business-team-led integration support to newly acquired entities.
- Liquidity risk in a working-capital-intensive model — Lack of available liquid financial assets such as cash may cause difficulties in achieving projected growth because the business is working capital intensive. IPO proceeds provided liquidity for growth plans, alongside measures to drive revenue growth and optimise costs to improve cash flows.
- Supply chain disruption / dependence on suppliers — The Company has no control over the supply of products from suppliers, which could be impacted by a number of factors; contingency plans allow transfer of goods from alternate locations within the group.
- Technology and cyber security risk — Loss of data and unauthorised access to IT systems from a security breach could adversely impact operations - material given the platform runs on a proprietary ERP and digital ordering stack. Mitigated through antivirus, firewalls, remote data backups and the latest software versions.
- People risk and attrition — Human capital is a key pillar and high attrition rates could impair performance; retention is managed through learning and skill-development workshops, engagement initiatives, the Entero Cares programme, rewards/recognition and cross-functional mobility for high performers.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Claims to be "One of India’s Largest & Fastest Growing Healthcare Supply Chain Company" and "Amongst the top three healthcare products distributors in India in terms of revenue", with the "Fastest scale-up of operations among healthcare products distributors in India with track record of 51 acquisitions".
- Core thesis is consolidation of a highly fragmented market: the deck (source: Prospectus) shows the share of the top 3 in pharma distribution at 8-10% in India (FY23 numbers) versus 90-95% for the top 3 in the US, 40-45% for the top 4 in China and 95-97% for the top 5 in Germany.
- Target Addressable Market put at $33.2bn (FY23) growing at a 10-11% market CAGR (FY23-FY28), with large/national distributors' share of total distributor sales rising from 8-10% in FY23 to 20-30% by FY28 (CAGR 25-30%).
- Differentiated model offers both demand fulfilment (end-to-end distribution) and demand generation (integrated commercial solutions — medical representatives, marketing strategy, channel management) to healthcare brands and manufacturers.
- Deck reports Entero growing well ahead of the market — organic LFL growth versus IPM growth of 1.4x-1.8x in every quarter shown from Q1FY26 through Q1FY27.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Divestment] Like-for-like growth is defined as including "impact of revenue recorded on net margin basis and divestment of a subsidiary" — the deck discloses the divestment only through this definition and gives no further detail on which subsidiary or the consideration.
- [Exceptional item] FY26 carried an exceptional item of Rs 8.2 Cr described as a "One-off impact of New Labour Code in India".
- [Governance] Board is chaired by a Non-Executive Independent Director (Sujesh Vasudevan), with two promoter executives (Prabhat Agrawal, MD & CEO; Prem Sethi, Whole-time Director & COO) and two nominee directors of the healthcare-focused investor.
- [Minority interest] Non-controlling interest is a large share of consolidated profit — Rs 13.9 Cr of Q1FY27's Rs 52.1 Cr PAT, leaving Rs 38.2 Cr to owners — a structural consequence of buying majority (not full) stakes in acquired distributors.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Entero is a pan-India B2B distributor of pharmaceutical, surgical, OTC/FMCG and other healthcare and allied products, sourcing from healthcare manufacturers and fulfilling to retail pharmacies, hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, wholesalers and diagnostic laboratories. It operates a hub-and-spoke warehouse network with end-to-end cold chain infrastructure and proprietary technology (in-house ERP, the Entero Direct ordering platform and the HealthEdge retailer-engagement initiative) that provides real-time inventory visibility, intelligent procurement, demand forecasting and warehouse optimisation. During FY26 the Company extended beyond pharmaceutical distribution into MedTech - diagnostics, medical devices, cardiology, orthopaedics, consumables and imaging - through a mix of organic initiatives and acquisitions, and also offers manufacturers integrated commercial solutions spanning sales, marketing, promotion and supply-chain management.

- **Pharmaceutical distribution:** Pharma / FMCG / Surgical / OTC SKUs, Specialty pharmaceuticals, Trade generics, Institutional healthcare supply
- **MedTech:** In-vitro diagnostics (IVD), Diagnostic reagents and equipment, Cardiology products, Orthopaedics, Imaging-related products, Medical devices, Medical consumables
- **Technology platforms:** In-house ERP systems, Entero Direct, HealthEdge
- **Commercial solutions:** Demand generation, medical sales and marketing, channel engagement and end-to-end distribution for manufacturers

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- ACQUIRE - leverage market consolidation by acquiring high-quality regional and local healthcare distributors that strengthen geographic presence, customer relationships and product portfolio, then integrate them onto a unified operating platform (common technology, supply chain, procurement).
- EXPAND - strengthen the distribution network by increasing customer reach, expanding hub-and-spoke infrastructure and raising wallet share through a broader product portfolio and technology-enabled customer engagement.
- PARTNER - deliver integrated commercial solutions to manufacturers spanning sales, marketing, promotion and supply chain management, so brands accelerate market access and patient reach.
- MedTech pivot - build scale in a structurally higher-margin, fragmented segment (IVD, cardiology, orthopaedics, imaging, consumables, specialty devices), progressively shifting from fulfilment-led arrangements to higher-value commercial roles and exclusive pan-India distribution partnerships.
- Shift from acquisition to integration - having completed a significant phase of acquisitions, focus moves to synergy realisation, operational efficiency and maximising returns from the expanded platform.
- Technology as an operating pillar - in-house ERP, Entero Direct and HealthEdge to drive inventory efficiency, fill rates, data-driven decisions and smooth onboarding of acquired businesses.
- Capital efficiency - disciplined inventory management, optimised procurement and tighter collections to shorten the net working capital cycle and sustain positive operating cash generation.
- Organic growth through deeper penetration of existing customers, wallet-share expansion and new customer addition in key geographies.
- The Board chose not to recommend any dividend for the year under review in order to conserve the resources of the Company, retaining earnings to fund the growth platform; a Dividend Distribution Policy has nonetheless been adopted under the SEBI Listing Regulations and is published on the Company's website. No amount is proposed to be transferred to the General Reserve. The Company has not accepted any deposits from the public or members, and had no principal or interest on public deposits outstanding as on March 31, 2026. There was no change in authorised share capital during the year; the only issued-capital movement came from the allotment of 3,230 equity shares on exercise of options under the Entero Employees Stock Option Plan, 2023, which is administered by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and under which 83,960 fresh options were granted during the year - i.e. equity issuance is confined to employee incentives rather than dilutive fundraising. Governance of capital is framed by a Board of eight in which all statutory committees except the Risk Management Committee are chaired by Independent Directors, and by a Managing Director and CFO certification to the Board on the accuracy of financial statements and adequacy of internal financial controls.
- BRSR is prepared on a consolidated basis covering Entero Healthcare Solutions Limited and its 48 subsidiaries, all of which are indicated as participating in the listed entity's business responsibility initiatives.
- Material issue identified as a risk - GHG (Green House Gas) emissions.
- Material issue identified as a risk - managing fleet fuel, reflecting the emissions and cost exposure of a nationwide physical distribution fleet.
- Material issue identified as an opportunity - employee welfare, on the rationale that a supportive workplace environment is essential to attracting and retaining talent and boosting morale.
- Material issue identified as an opportunity - business ethics.
- CSR is applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 to the Company and to eight named subsidiaries (Chethana Pharma, Chirag Medicare Solutions, R S M Pharma, Sai Pharma Distributors, Peerless Biotech, Curever Pharma, Ace Cardiopathy Solutions and Bioaide Technologies).
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place across stakeholder groups, including a dedicated investor grievance email, the Stakeholders' Relationship Committee and SEBI SCORES route, a published Whistleblower Policy, an Employee Code of Conduct and a Supplier Code of Conduct; complaints across the responsible-business principles were reported nil for FY 2025-26 other than one SCORES filing that was an internal HR matter and stands closed.
- No external assurance provider was appointed for the BRSR and no type of assurance was obtained.
- Operations are exclusively within India with no export activity; the reported permanent-employee turnover rate remains high (in the mid-to-high thirties percent), which the Company addresses through its retention and engagement programmes.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Entero's expansion is network- and acquisition-led rather than plant-led: it is a distribution platform, and the annual report describes no manufacturing capex project, no commissioning schedule and no rupee capex programme. Physical expansion is the fulfilment network - a pan-India footprint of 135 warehouses servicing more than 100,000 retail pharmacies and over 3,500 hospitals across 523 districts, carrying a portfolio exceeding 95,000 SKUs sourced from over 3,300 manufacturers. Alongside this, the Company invests in its proprietary technology stack (in-house ERP, the Entero Direct real-time inventory and ordering platform, and the HealthEdge retailer-engagement initiative), which also serves as the mechanism for absorbing acquired businesses into the operating framework. The principal expansion vector during FY26 was the MedTech vertical, a higher-margin adjacency where capabilities range from fulfilment-led arrangements to value-added commercial roles and exclusive pan-India distribution partnerships; post integration, management expects MedTech to cross Rs 1,000 crore in annualised revenue in FY27. Inorganic expansion during FY 2025-26 took the form of seven new subsidiary acquisitions: 80% of Bioaide Technologies Private Limited, 80% of Anand Medilink Private Limited, 70% of Sai RK Pharma Private Limited, 70% of Well Wisher Pharma Private Limited, 70% of Ramson Medical Distributors Private Limited, 60% of Ace Cardiopathy Solutions Private Limited and 51.51% of Anand Chemiceutics Private Limited. The Company also raised its holding in Peerless Biotech Private Limited by a further 16% to 76%. Structural clean-up accompanied the build-out: Chethana Pharma Distributors Private Limited and CPD Pharma Private Limited were transferred to fellow wholly owned subsidiary Rada Medisolutions Private Limited and merged into it via the fast-track route with an appointed date of April 15, 2025; the entire 100% stake in Suprabhat Pharmaceuticals Private Limited was sold back to its erstwhile promoters; and three non-operational entities - Zennx Software Private Limited, Quromed Lifesciences Private Limited and Rimedio Pharma Private Limited - were struck off with effect from May 01, 2025, June 02, 2025 and June 05, 2025 respectively. As on March 31, 2026 the Company had 48 subsidiaries and no associates or joint ventures.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic pharmaceutical market grew ~10% in FY26 to around Rs 2.56 lakh crore and the sector is expected to maintain its growth momentum in FY27; Entero derives revenue from this domestic market, characterised by stable and resilient demand.
- Indian pharmaceutical market valued at ~US$55 billion in 2025 and projected to reach US$120-130 billion by 2030, driven by specialty medicines, biologics and complex therapies.
- Indian medical devices market at ~US$14-16 billion growing 12-14% per annum; Entero's MedTech push is aligned to these tailwinds and is intended to diversify revenue mix and enhance profitability.
- Total addressable market for pharmaceutical and medical device distribution in India was ~US$33 billion in FY23 and is expected to grow at a 10-11% CAGR through FY28.
- Roughly 90% of the distribution market is still serviced by small, region-specific distributors; rising compliance standards, technology adoption and consolidation imperatives are expected to raise the organised share - the core structural driver for Entero.
- MedTech offers structurally superior margins relative to pharmaceutical distribution and is expected to become an increasing contributor to consolidated profitability as initiatives scale.
- Margin expansion is expected to be driven by ongoing business-mix improvement, integration benefits and operating leverage as the business scales further.
- GLP-1 is an emerging sub-segment: the domestic market is expected to grow nearly fivefold from ~Rs 1,000-1,200 crore in 2025 to Rs 4,500-5,000 crore by 2030 after a more-than-50% price decline following March 2026 patent expiry - management says this can create incremental distribution opportunities over the medium term.
- MedTech import dependence (~75-80% of device consumption by value) plus PLI for Medical Devices and the National Medical Device Policy 2023 are lifting domestic manufacturing and Tier-II/Tier-III distribution penetration.
- Organic like-for-like growth of 15.6% in FY26 versus ~10% IPM growth reflects deeper penetration of existing customers, wallet-share expansion and new customer additions; management is confident of sustaining this organic trajectory.
- PLI scheme, expanded affordable-medicine programmes, rising health insurance penetration, growing urbanisation and increasing chronic disease prevalence underpin long-term demand.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Entero delivered 31.5% like-for-like FY26 growth and 4% EBITDA margins, guided to 23% organic growth and 5% margins in FY27 driven by MedTech scale (15% of revenue) and GLP-1 cold-chain dominance, though reported PAT is distorted by a one-off 38% minority interest spike that normalizes to ~25% next year.

open.item: The MedTech business is expected to contribute more than Rs 1,000 crore of annualised revenue in FY27, expanding the addressable market and strengthening the margin profile.
Post integration, the MedTech vertical is expected to cross Rs 1,000 crore in annualised revenue in FY27.

For FY27 the focus will be on driving profitable growth, strengthening cash generation and further improving operational efficiency, with integration and synergy realisation from the completed acquisition phase.

Expand presence into adjacent product segments - medical devices, diagnostics, trade generics, specialty pharmaceuticals, OTC products and wellness categories - to complement the core business and enhance customer stickiness.

Continue to evaluate inorganic growth opportunities in a selective and disciplined manner to enhance geographic reach, broaden capabilities and augment the product and service offering, while first maximising synergies from the platform already built.
Management will continue to focus on further improving working capital cycles as the business scales.
Consolidate and deepen the integration of the FY26 MedTech acquisitions across the business and drive synergies across the pharmaceutical and MedTech distribution networks.

currentContext.expansion: Entero's expansion is network- and acquisition-led rather than plant-led: it is a distribution platform, and the annual report describes no manufacturing capex project, no commissioning schedule and no rupee capex programme. Physical expansion is the fulfilment network - a pan-India footprint of 135 warehouses servicing more than 100,000 retail pharmacies and over 3,500 hospitals across 523 districts, carrying a portfolio exceeding 95,000 SKUs sourced from over 3,300 manufacturers. Alongside this, the Company invests in its proprietary technology stack (in-house ERP, the Entero Direct real-time inventory and ordering platform, and the HealthEdge retailer-engagement initiative), which also serves as the mechanism for absorbing acquired businesses into the operating framework. The principal expansion vector during FY26 was the MedTech vertical, a higher-margin adjacency where capabilities range from fulfilment-led arrangements to value-added commercial roles and exclusive pan-India distribution partnerships; post integration, management expects MedTech to cross Rs 1,000 crore in annualised revenue in FY27. Inorganic expansion during FY 2025-26 took the form of seven new subsidiary acquisitions: 80% of Bioaide Technologies Private Limited, 80% of Anand Medilink Private Limited, 70% of Sai RK Pharma Private Limited, 70% of Well Wisher Pharma Private Limited, 70% of Ramson Medical Distributors Private Limited, 60% of Ace Cardiopathy Solutions Private Limited and 51.51% of Anand Chemiceutics Private Limited. The Company also raised its holding in Peerless Biotech Private Limited by a further 16% to 76%. Structural clean-up accompanied the build-out: Chethana Pharma Distributors Private Limited and CPD Pharma Private Limited were transferred to fellow wholly owned subsidiary Rada Medisolutions Private Limited and merged into it via the fast-track route with an appointed date of April 15, 2025; the entire 100% stake in Suprabhat Pharmaceuticals Private Limited was sold back to its erstwhile promoters; and three non-operational entities - Zennx Software Private Limited, Quromed Lifesciences Private Limited and Rimedio Pharma Private Limited - were struck off with effect from May 01, 2025, June 02, 2025 and June 05, 2025 respectively. As on March 31, 2026 the Company had 48 subsidiaries and no associates or joint ventures.

risks.note: The business is exposed to distributing expired, defective or counterfeit products, transportation damage and customer returns, which could cause financial losses, reputational damage and product liability claims - and any claim, regardless of validity, can erode customer trust. Mitigation is buying directly from manufacturers meeting agreed quality standards, with defects replaced by the manufacturer.

risks.risk: Operational disruption to warehouses and logistics
risks.note: Any disruption to warehouse operations, or to the development of new warehousing and logistics facilities - including natural disasters or catastrophic events - could materially impact the business. Redundancy across a nationwide network of 100+ distribution warehouses is the stated buffer.

Growth is acquisition-led, so failure to identify, complete and successfully integrate acquisitions, or acquisitions failing to deliver internal results, would directly hit financial performance. Mitigated by a dedicated M&A team targeting territorial expansion/dominance or unique product mix, plus business-team-led integration support to newly acquired entities.

risks.risk: Liquidity risk in a working-capital-intensive model
risks.note: Lack of available liquid financial assets such as cash may cause difficulties in achieving projected growth because the business is working capital intensive. IPO proceeds provided liquidity for growth plans, alongside measures to drive revenue growth and optimise costs to improve cash flows.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption / dependence on suppliers
risks.note: The Company has no control over the supply of products from suppliers, which could be impacted by a number of factors; contingency plans allow transfer of goods from alternate locations within the group.

Loss of data and unauthorised access to IT systems from a security breach could adversely impact operations - material given the platform runs on a proprietary ERP and digital ordering stack. Mitigated through antivirus, firewalls, remote data backups and the latest software versions.

Human capital is a key pillar and high attrition rates could impair performance; retention is managed through learning and skill-development workshops, engagement initiatives, the Entero Cares programme, rewards/recognition and cross-functional mobility for high performers.

one-line thesis: Entero delivered 31.5% like-for-like FY26 growth and 4% EBITDA margins, guided to 23% organic growth and 5% margins in FY27 driven by MedTech scale (15% of revenue) and GLP-1 cold-chain dominance, though reported PAT is distorted by a one-off 38% minority interest spike that normalizes to ~25% next year.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic pharmaceutical market grew ~10% in FY26 to around Rs 2.56 lakh crore and the sector is expected to maintain its growth momentum in FY27; Entero derives revenue from this domestic market, characterised by stable and resilient demand.
- Indian pharmaceutical market valued at ~US$55 billion in 2025 and projected to reach US$120-130 billion by 2030, driven by specialty medicines, biologics and complex therapies.
- Indian medical devices market at ~US$14-16 billion growing 12-14% per annum; Entero's MedTech push is aligned to these tailwinds and is intended to diversify revenue mix and enhance profitability.
- Total addressable market for pharmaceutical and medical device distribution in India was ~US$33 billion in FY23 and is expected to grow at a 10-11% CAGR through FY28.
- Roughly 90% of the distribution market is still serviced by small, region-specific distributors; rising compliance standards, technology adoption and consolidation imperatives are expected to raise the organised share - the core structural driver for Entero.
- MedTech offers structurally superior margins relative to pharmaceutical distribution and is expected to become an increasing contributor to consolidated profitability as initiatives scale.
- Margin expansion is expected to be driven by ongoing business-mix improvement, integration benefits and operating leverage as the business scales further.
- GLP-1 is an emerging sub-segment: the domestic market is expected to grow nearly fivefold from ~Rs 1,000-1,200 crore in 2025 to Rs 4,500-5,000 crore by 2030 after a more-than-50% price decline following March 2026 patent expiry - management says this can create incremental distribution opportunities over the medium term.
- MedTech import dependence (~75-80% of device consumption by value) plus PLI for Medical Devices and the National Medical Device Policy 2023 are lifting domestic manufacturing and Tier-II/Tier-III distribution penetration.
- Organic like-for-like growth of 15.6% in FY26 versus ~10% IPM growth reflects deeper penetration of existing customers, wallet-share expansion and new customer additions; management is confident of sustaining this organic trajectory.
- PLI scheme, expanded affordable-medicine programmes, rising health insurance penetration, growing urbanisation and increasing chronic disease prevalence underpin long-term demand.

- [Divestment] Like-for-like growth is defined as including "impact of revenue recorded on net margin basis and divestment of a subsidiary" — the deck discloses the divestment only through this definition and gives no further detail on which subsidiary or the consideration.

- [Governance] Board is chaired by a Non-Executive Independent Director (Sujesh Vasudevan), with two promoter executives (Prabhat Agrawal, MD & CEO; Prem Sethi, Whole-time Director & COO) and two nominee directors of the healthcare-focused investor.
- [Minority interest] Non-controlling interest is a large share of consolidated profit — Rs 13.9 Cr of Q1FY27's Rs 52.1 Cr PAT, leaving Rs 38.2 Cr to owners — a structural consequence of buying majority (not full) stakes in acquired distributors.

one-line thesis: Entero delivered 31.5% like-for-like FY26 growth and 4% EBITDA margins, guided to 23% organic growth and 5% margins in FY27 driven by MedTech scale (15% of revenue) and GLP-1 cold-chain dominance, though reported PAT is distorted by a one-off 38% minority interest spike that normalizes to ~25% next year.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR 6,591cr (+31.5% LFL); EBITDA INR 266cr (4% margin, +67bps); PAT INR 146cr (+36%, distorted by Q4 one-off minority interest); Order Book N/A (distribution model); Net Debt rising post-IPO fund deployment with finance costs expected to stabilize then decline.
guidance: Revenue growth 23% (organic, ex-new M&A); EBITDA margin 5%; Order inflow steady via global MedTech partnerships; Capex focused on MedTech asset placement (reagent rental model).
order book & pipeline: N/A for distribution; however, MedTech reagent-rental contracts (5-year tenure) drive recurring revenue visibility; platform serves 100k+ pharmacies, 3.6k hospitals, 3.3k manufacturers.
segment / subsidiary detail: Pharma remains core but MedTech now >INR 1,000cr annualized revenue (15% of total, targeting 20% in 2-3 years); MedTech margins significantly higher due to commercial agency role vs pure fulfillment.
growth verticals / optionality: Organic scale in MedTech sub-segments (Imaging, Neuropsychiatry, Orthopedics); GLP-1 category capture (currently INR 10-12cr/month, ~5% industry share) via exclusive cold-chain infrastructure; potential upward guidance revision if new M&A occurs.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin expanded 78bps FY26 (10.3%) and 110bps Q4 (10.9%) due to scale economics and commercial agency roles; FY27 EBITDA guided at 5% (+50bps vs Q4) despite normalization of minority interest; depreciation rising due to MedTech asset placement.
capex / expansion: Asset-light overall but specific capex/depreciation increase in MedTech IVD segment for machines placed under reagent-rental models; no heavy infrastructure capex mentioned.
capital allocation: Pause on new M&A for 6-8 months to digest 7 recent acquisitions (3 MedTech); focus on organic ROIC improvement; put option liabilities recognized under IndAS impacting net worth presentation.
risks & watch-items: Minority interest volatility (normalized from 38% to ~25%); working capital cycle sensitivity to MedTech mix (higher receivable days); key person risk in acquired entities mitigated by 1-year lock-ins and skin-in-the-game.
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'chewing' acquired assets over new deals; transparent on accounting distortions (put options, minority spikes); bullish on MedTech synergies.
non-obvious takeaways: Reported net worth flattish due to IndAS put option liability recognition rather than operational decline; Q4 minority interest spike was a one-off due to preponed government project sales in a partial-owned subsidiary; GLP-1 distribution is a hidden moat due to cold-chain barriers.

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.
